newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering's Pohle sees 1997 profit up 8-9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Schering's Pohle sees 1997 profit up 8-9 pct.

text.p: Klaus Pohle, chief financial officer at German pharmaceuticals group Schering AG said on Tuesday he expected the company's profit to grow by eight or nine percent in 1997 with a double-digit increase in cash flow.

Pohle also predicted in a telephone conference with analysts that Schering's group sales would be around 5.9 billion marks ($3.5 billion), with sales of the company's highly successful multiple sclerosis drug Betaferon reaching 590 million marks.
He added in answer to a question that Schering did not expect any additional restructuring provisions in 1997 alongside those which had already been made.

"We said before we published today's unexpectedly- high figure that we expected high single-digit growth. Well, we still expect growth of between eight and nine percent, which will leave us at around 400 million marks," Pohle said.
"We expect double-digit scale increase in our cash-flow in 1997," he added.
Earlier, Schering reported a jump of 46 percent in its 1996 profit, taking it to a record level of 362 million marks.
On the MS drug Betaferon, Pohle said, "We expect sales of 590 million marks of Betaferon in 1997 and we expect a better performance in Britain."
He added that he did not anticipate any further restructuring provisions other than the 60 million marks reserved in the 1996 balance sheet.
